cohort: The study included 73 singleton pregnancies from donated embryos and 136 singleton pregnancies from autologous frozen-thawed embryo transfer (FET), involving women under 44 years old.
finding: Pregnancies conceived with donated embryos were associated with a significantly higher risk of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDPs), particularly severe forms, compared to autologous frozen-thawed embryo transfer (FET) pregnancies.
mod_finding: C-sections were significantly more frequent in donated-embryo pregnancies (47.3%) compared to autologous FET pregnancies (29.2%).
birth_weight: Measured and found comparable between groups.
gest_age: Measured and found comparable (in terms of prematurity and SGA/LGA outcomes) between groups.
